object: A simultaneously selected family of normalized complementary cut pairs on the diagonal complement universe of G_NEQ.
qoi: The minimum number k of binary cut coordinates needed so every unequal label pair is separated, together with the maximum discrimination available to the cardinality-only first-order signature argument.

included: G_NEQ on N labels with N>=2
joint binary signatures of the N diagonal generator traces
exact finite construction and counterexample-first calibration
capacity-only pigeonhole arguments on a fixed distinguished trace set
excluded: arbitrary target graphs or arbitrary full semi-filter geometries
higher-order tuple, intersection, or closure-state signatures
an unrestricted-cover lower bound above logarithmic order
any theorem about P versus NP

representation.coordinate: For cut S_j, bit_j(u)=1 iff u is in S_j.
representation.coverage_rule: A normalized cut pair covers every semi-filter above unequal edge (u,v) whenever sig(u) and sig(v) differ in that coordinate; if all coordinates agree, the canonical semi-filter above (u,v) is not covered by the family.
discarded: non-generator semi-filter closure structure outside G_NEQ

frozen_predictions.statement: For every N>=2 and every normalized cut family, all G_NEQ unequal-pair obligations are covered iff the N joint binary signatures are injective.
The exact minimum coordinate count in this G_NEQ representation is ceil(log2 N).
At k=ceil(log2 N)-1, capacity 2^k is strictly below N, so a collision and an uncovered unequal pair are forced.

A lower-bound argument using only cardinality of binary signatures on M distinguished traces saturates at ceil(log2 M); if M is polynomial in graph side size N, this capacity-only argument is O(log N).

frozen_falsifiers.condition: An exact small-N search finds a covering normalized family with k<ceil(log2 N).
The constructive length-ceil(log2 N) codebook leaves any unequal pair unseparated.
Direct cut-membership coverage and signature-inequality coverage disagree on any enumerated family.
A cardinality-only binary-signature argument distinguishes more than 2^k states with k coordinates.

planned_claim_if_predictions_pass: Within normalized G_NEQ cut families, joint binary signatures exactly repair C024's lost integrality and recover ceil(log2 N), but the cardinality-only first-order capacity argument is exhausted at logarithmic order and supplies no super-logarithmic route evidence.
